stimuli.text: A block of mass 3 kg on a 37° incline is connected by a light string over a light, frictionless pulley at the top of the incline to a hanging block of mass 3 kg. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the block and the incline is 0.25. The system is released from rest, and the hanging block descends.
A block of mass 1 kg on a horizontal frictionless surface is attached to a spring. Its position is $$x(t) = 0.09\cos(3t)$$, with x in meters and t in seconds.
Students measure the period of a simple pendulum for several string lengths, using small amplitudes.
A hoop (I = MR²) and a solid sphere (I = ⅖MR²) of equal mass M and radius R are released from rest at the top of the same ramp of height 2.9 m. Both roll without slipping.

questions.stem: A 73 kg person stands on a scale in an elevator that is accelerating upward at 3 m/s². What does the scale read?

options.why: Check the direction of the acceleration.
Correct. The scale reads the normal force: N − mg = ma (up positive).
The acceleration changes the normal force.
Include gravity.

questions.stem: A planet has 3 times Earth's mass and 3 times Earth's radius. What is the gravitational field strength at its surface? (Earth's is 9.8 N/kg.)

options.why: Correct. g ∝ M/R².
g decreases with radius.
g depends on 1/R², not 1/R.
The ratio is inverted.

questions.stem: A motor lifts a 460 kg load 4 m at constant speed in 6 s. What average power does it deliver?

options.why: Correct. P = mgh/t.
P = W/t.
Include g.
That is the work; divide by time.

questions.stem: A curve of radius 40 m is banked so that a car at 13 m/s needs no friction. What is the banking angle?

options.why: Square the speed.
Measure the angle from the horizontal.
Correct. tan θ = v²/(rg).
Use tan θ = v²/(rg), from dividing the force components.

questions.stem: A spring with $$k = 280$$ N/m is compressed 0.2 m and launches a 0.8 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: Correct. ½kx² = ½mv².
Use energy: v = x√(k/m).
The ½ appears on both sides.
Take the square root.

questions.stem: A particle's position is $$x(t) = -2t^3 - 4t^2 - 1t$$, with x in meters and t in seconds. What is its acceleration at $$t = 4$$ s?

options.why: The derivative of 2bt is 2b, which also remains.
Bring each exponent down as a factor when differentiating.
Correct. Differentiate twice: a = 6at + 2b.
That is the velocity; differentiate again.

questions.explanation: a(t) = -12t - 8, so at t = 4 the value is -56.

questions.stem: A force $$F(x) = 3x^2$$ N acts along the x-axis. How much work does it do on an object moving from $$x = 1$$ m to $$x = 2$$ m?

options.why: Integrate; do not just evaluate F.
The force is not constant.
Correct. W = ∫F dx.
Divide by n + 1 when integrating.

questions.stem: A block slides down a 25° incline. The coefficient of kinetic friction is 0.3. What is the magnitude of its acceleration?

options.why: The component along the incline is mg sin θ.
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Friction acts up the slope.
Correct. a = g(sin θ − μk cos θ).

questions.stem: Two springs with constants 80 N/m and 70 N/m are connected in parallel and support a 3 kg mass at rest. How far do they stretch in total?

options.why: The force is the weight, mg.
Both springs share the load.
Series and parallel rules are reversed.
Correct. k_eq = k₁ + k₂.

questions.stem: A ball rolls off a horizontal ledge 7.5 m high at 6 m/s. How far from the base of the ledge does it land?

options.why: Correct. Fall time from the height, times the horizontal speed.
Take the square root for the time.
Fall time is √(2h/g).
Horizontal and vertical motion are independent.

questions.stem: A 0.2 kg mass oscillates on a spring with $$k = 25$$ N/m. What is the period?

options.why: The ratio is m/k.
Include the 2π.
That is the frequency.
Correct. T = 2π√(m/k).

questions.stem: A wheel spinning at 18 rad/s slows uniformly to rest in 5 s. How many revolutions does it make while stopping?

options.why: Recheck the average.
Correct. Δθ = ½ω₀t, then divide by 2π.
That is in radians; convert to revolutions.
The average angular speed is ω₀/2.

questions.stem: A 0.3 kg ball hits a wall at 18 m/s and rebounds at 11 m/s. The contact lasts 0.04 s. What is the average force from the wall?

options.why: The velocity reverses, so the speeds add.
Include the rebound.
Divide by time.
Correct. Δp = m(v_f − v_i) with the direction reversed.

questions.stem: A system obeys $$\frac{d^2x}{dt^2} = -9x$$. What is the period of its motion?

options.why: T = 2π/ω.
ω is the square root of the coefficient.
Correct. ω = √9 = 3 rad/s, T = 2π/ω.
T = 2π/ω, not 2πω.

questions.stem: A car moving at 28 m/s brakes with a constant deceleration of 2 m/s². How far does it travel before stopping?

options.why: Divide by 2a, not a.
Correct. Use v² = v₀² + 2aΔx with v = 0.
That is the stopping time in seconds.
Δx = v₀²/(2a).

questions.stem: A 1 kg cart moving at 8 m/s collides with and sticks to a 6 kg cart at rest. What is their speed after the collision?

options.why: Kinetic energy is not conserved here.
Correct. Momentum is conserved; kinetic energy is not.
Use m₁v₁ for the initial momentum.
The carts share the momentum.

questions.explanation: v_f = 1·8/7 = 1.14 m/s; kinetic energy lost = 27.4 J.

questions.stem: An oscillator's position is $$x(t) = 0.12\cos(14t)$$ m. What is its maximum speed?

options.why: Multiply by ω.
Correct. v_max = Aω.
That is a_max.
v_max = Aω.

questions.stem: A ball is launched from level ground at 25 m/s at 70° above the horizontal. Ignoring air resistance, what is its horizontal range?

options.why: Correct. Treat horizontal and vertical motion separately.
That is the maximum range, at 45°.
Use the full time of flight.
Range uses sin 2θ.

questions.explanation: v₀x = 8.55 m/s, v₀y = 23.5 m/s. R = v₀² sin 2θ/g = 41 m.

questions.stem: An object of mass 1 kg falls from rest with a drag force $$F = -bv$$, where $$b = 0.1$$ kg/s. What is the time constant of its approach to terminal speed?

options.why: That is the terminal speed.
τ has units of seconds: m/b.
τ = m/b.
Correct. From m dv/dt = mg − bv, τ = m/b.

questions.explanation: v_T = mg/b = 98 m/s and τ = m/b = 10 s.

questions.stem: A spring with $$k = 300$$ N/m is compressed 0.16 m and launches a 0.7 kg block across a frictionless surface. What is the block's speed after leaving the spring?

options.why: Take the square root.
The ½ appears on both sides.
Correct. ½kx² = ½mv².
Use energy: v = x√(k/m).

questions.stem: Masses of 9 kg and 4 kg hang on either side of a light, frictionless pulley. What is the magnitude of their acceleration?

options.why: The whole system accelerates: divide by both masses.
The masses are connected, so a is less than g.
The fraction is inverted.
Correct. a = (m₁ − m₂)g/(m₁ + m₂).

questions.stem: A solid cylinder rolls without slipping from rest down a ramp of height 0.6 m. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Some energy goes into rotation.
Correct. mgh = ½mv²(1 + β) with I = ½MR².
Rotational energy is ½Iω² = ½βmv².
That is only correct for a hoop.

questions.stem: A 6 kg block on a horizontal table is connected by a string over a light pulley to a hanging 3 kg block. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the table and the block is 0.3. What is the acceleration of the blocks?

options.why: Both blocks accelerate; divide by the total mass.
Correct. Net force (m₂g − μm₁g) divided by the total mass.
Include friction on the table block.
Friction opposes the motion.

questions.stem: A 5 kg object at rest experiences a net force $$F(t) = 3t^2$$ N from $$t = 0$$ to $$t = 4$$ s. What is its final speed?

options.why: The force is not constant.
Divide by the mass to get speed.
Correct. Impulse ∫F dt equals the change in momentum.
Integrate the force over time.

questions.explanation: J = ∫F dt = 64 N·s; v = J/m = 12.8 m/s.

questions.stem: A 8 kg ball moving at +5 m/s collides elastically head-on with a 9 kg ball at rest. What is the velocity of the 9 kg ball afterward (positive in the original direction)?

options.why: That would be a sticking collision.
Correct. Elastic: conserve momentum and kinetic energy (relative velocity reverses).
Kinetic energy is conserved too.
Only equal masses exchange velocities.

questions.explanation: v₁' = (m₁ − m₂)v/(m₁ + m₂) = -0.294 m/s; v₂' = 2m₁v/(m₁ + m₂) = 4.71 m/s.

questions.stem: A uniform 3 m beam weighing 400 N rests on supports at both ends. A 800 N load sits 1 m from the left end. What force does the right support exert?

options.why: Include the beam's weight at its center.
Correct. Take torques about the left support.
That is the left support's force.
The load is not at the center.

questions.stem: A rod lies along the x-axis from $$x = 0$$ to $$x = 1$$ m and has linear mass density $$\lambda = kx^2$$. Where is its center of mass?

options.why: The rod is not uniform.
Correct. x_cm = ∫xλ dx / ∫λ dx.
The exponents are n + 2 and n + 1.
Integrate x·xⁿ and xⁿ correctly.

questions.stem: A block starts from rest and slides 7 m down a 30° incline with coefficient of kinetic friction 0.1. What is its speed at the bottom?

options.why: Correct. mgh − μmg cos θ·L = ½mv².
Friction depends on the normal force, mg cos θ.
Use the vertical drop, L sin θ.
Friction removes energy.

questions.stem: A uniform rod of length 2.1 m is pivoted at one end and released from rest in a horizontal position. What is its angular acceleration just after release?

options.why: Use τ = Iα with I = ML²/3.
Correct. τ = Mg(L/2) and I = ML²/3 give α = 3g/(2L).
τ = MgL/2.
The weight acts at L/2.

questions.stem: An object's acceleration is $$a(t) = 6t$$ m/s². At $$t = 0$$ it has velocity 4 m/s and is at $$x = 0$$. What is its position at $$t = 3$$ s?

options.why: Integrating tⁿ divides by n + 1.
Include the initial velocity.
That is the velocity.
Correct. Integrate twice, using the initial conditions.

questions.stem: A planet has mass $$7 \times 10^{23}$$ kg and radius $$4 \times 10^{7}$$ m. What is the escape speed from its surface? ($$G = 6.67 \times 10^{-11}$$ N·m²/kg²)

options.why: Take the square root.
That is the circular orbit speed; escape needs √2 times more.
Potential energy uses 1/R.
Correct. ½mv² = GMm/R.

questions.stem: A 2500 kg car heading east at 19 m/s collides with a 3000 kg car heading north at 18 m/s, and they lock together. What is their speed just after the collision?

options.why: Weight each velocity by its mass.
Divide by the total mass.
Correct. Conserve momentum in x and y separately, then combine.
Momentum is a vector; add components at right angles.

questions.stem: A uniform disk of mass 2 kg and radius 0.3 m spins at 12 rad/s on a frictionless axle. A 0.5 kg lump of clay is dropped onto the rim and sticks. What is the new angular speed?

options.why: The clay's inertia is mR².
Use rotational inertias, not masses.
Kinetic energy is not conserved in a sticking collision.
Correct. Angular momentum is conserved: I_iω_i = I_fω_f.

questions.stem: A uniform disk of mass 8 kg and radius 0.5 m spins at 9 rad/s on a frictionless axle. A 0.75 kg lump of clay is dropped onto the rim and sticks. What is the new angular speed?

options.why: The clay's inertia is mR².
Correct. Angular momentum is conserved: I_iω_i = I_fω_f.
Kinetic energy is not conserved in a sticking collision.
Use rotational inertias, not masses.

questions.stem: A uniform disk of mass 4 kg and radius 0.2 m rotates about an axis perpendicular to it, 1.5 m from its center. What is its rotational inertia?

options.why: The axis is not through the center.
The parallel-axis term is Md².
Include the disk's own I about its center.
Correct. Parallel-axis theorem: I = ½MR² + Md².

questions.stem: The potential energy of a particle is $$U(x) = 1x^3 - 30x$$ J. At what positive x is the particle in stable equilibrium?

options.why: dU/dx = 3ax² − b.
Correct. Equilibrium where dU/dx = 0; stable at a minimum.
Set the derivative, not U, to zero.
Take the square root.

questions.explanation: dU/dx = 3x² − 30 = 0 gives x = 3.16 m; d²U/dx² > 0 there, so it is stable.

questions.stem: A 10 g bullet moving at 280 m/s embeds in a 3.8 kg block hanging from strings. How high does the block rise?

options.why: h = V²/(2g).
Kinetic energy is not conserved in the collision.
Find the block's speed after the collision first.
Correct. Momentum for the collision, then energy for the swing.

questions.explanation: V = 0.735 m/s after the collision; h = V²/(2g) = 0.0276 m.

questions.stem: A mass on a spring oscillates with angular frequency 3 rad/s and amplitude 0.16 m. What is its speed when it is 0.096 m from equilibrium?

options.why: That is the maximum speed, at x = 0.
Speed is greatest at equilibrium, not at the ends.
Use A² − x² under a square root.
Correct. v = ω√(A² − x²), from conservation of energy.

questions.stem: Satellite B orbits a planet in a circular orbit 4 times the radius of satellite A's circular orbit. What is the ratio of B's orbital speed to A's?

options.why: Correct. v = √(GM/r), so v ∝ r^(−1/2).
Farther satellites move more slowly.

questions.stem: A 3 kg mass hangs from a light string wrapped around a uniform disk pulley of mass 8 kg that turns on a frictionless axle. What is the acceleration of the mass?

options.why: I/R² = M/2.
The pulley's inertia reduces the acceleration.
Correct. a = mg/(m + M/2), using I = ½MR² and a = Rα.
For a disk, I/R² = M/2.

questions.explanation: mg − T = ma and TR = ½MR²(a/R) give a = 4.2 m/s².

questions.title: Block on an incline with a hanging mass

parts.prompt: Draw (describe) a free-body diagram for the 3 kg block, labeling each force.

rubric.criterion: Weight down, normal force perpendicular to the incline, tension up the incline.
Kinetic friction down the incline (opposite the motion).

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the acceleration of the system in terms of the masses, θ, μ and g, then calculate its value.

rubric.criterion: Newton's second law applied to each block (or the system).

parts.prompt: Calculate the tension in the string.
Calculate the speed of the blocks after the hanging block has descended 0.5 m, and the work done by friction on the incline block during that motion.

rubric.criterion: Work by friction, with a negative sign.

parts.prompt: Sketch (describe) graphs of position, velocity and acceleration versus time for one period, aligned vertically.

rubric.criterion: Position is a cosine starting at +A; velocity is a negative sine starting at 0.
rubric.example: x starts at 0.09 m; v starts at 0 and goes negative.

rubric.criterion: Acceleration starts at its negative maximum and is opposite in sign to position throughout.

parts.prompt: Derive expressions for v(t) and a(t), and determine the maximum speed and maximum acceleration.
Calculate the spring constant and the period.
Calculate the total mechanical energy and describe how kinetic and potential energy vary during one period.

rubric.example: K is maximum at x = 0 and zero at x = ±A; U is the reverse; the sum is constant. Each varies twice per period.

parts.prompt: Describe a procedure the students could use to measure the period accurately, including how to reduce uncertainty.

rubric.example: Time 10 swings with a stopwatch and divide by 10.

rubric.criterion: Keep the amplitude small and repeat trials.
rubric.example: Release from under about 10° and average several trials.

parts.prompt: Identify quantities to graph that would give a straight line, and explain how g can be found from the graph.
Plot (describe) the linearized data and draw a best-fit line. Use it to calculate an experimental value of g.
The students repeat the experiment with a much larger amplitude. Predict how the measured periods would change and explain.

rubric.criterion: Periods increase slightly; the small-angle approximation (sin θ ≈ θ) no longer holds.
rubric.example: The restoring torque is less than proportional to θ at large angles.

parts.prompt: Without calculating, predict which object reaches the bottom first. Justify your prediction using energy.

rubric.example: It has the smaller rotational inertia per MR².

rubric.criterion: Justification: less of its energy goes into rotation, so more is translational kinetic energy.

parts.prompt: Derive an expression for the speed at the bottom of an object with rotational inertia βMR², in terms of g, h and β.

rubric.criterion: Energy conservation including both forms of kinetic energy, with v = Rω.

parts.prompt: Calculate the speed of each object at the bottom.
Explain whether your derived expression is consistent with your prediction in part (a), and why neither speed depends on M or R.

rubric.criterion: Smaller β gives larger v, consistent with the prediction.
M and R cancel in the energy equation.
rubric.example: Only the shape factor β matters.
